title: Tesla, Gauss, Millitesla: MRI, Speakers and the Earth's Field
h1: Tesla and gauss — MRI, motors and geomagnetism on one scale
description: 1 T = 10 000 G. Earth's field is 0.5 G; a fridge magnet 50 G; a 3 T MRI is 30 000 G. Same physics, wildly different regimes.

hero: The SI tesla replaced the CGS gauss — but the factor of 10 000 keeps both alive in engineering practice.
body: Magnetic flux density spans nine orders of magnitude in everyday engineering, from geomagnetic anomalies (nanotesla) to fusion-reactor confinement (tens of tesla). Gauss and tesla coexist because each is convenient for its own regime.

> 1 T = 10 000 G = 10⁴ G
> 1 mT = 10 G
> 1 µT = 10 mG
> 1 nT = 10 µG (used in geomagnetism)

Tesla: MRI (1.5 T, 3 T, 7 T), particle physics magnets, generator air gaps. Gauss: audio speakers, magnetic separators, refrigerator magnets, hall-effect current sensors. Milligauss / microtesla: EMF shielding, health-standard compliance. Nanotesla: geomagnetic mapping, magnetometry.

A 3 T bore radiates a 5-gauss line typically 3–4 m from isocentre — the safety perimeter for pacemakers and ferrous carts. That 5 G = 0.5 mT = 500 µT, still 10 000× Earth's ambient. Skipping the gauss/tesla conversion when siting equipment can misplace the perimeter by metres.
Multiply tesla by 10 000 to get gauss. MRI in T, motors and sensors in G, geomagnetism in nT.

faqs.q: Is a 'gauss meter' actually measuring gauss?
faqs.a: Yes — Hall-effect probes usually report gauss (or milligauss for shielding work). Some scientific units auto-switch to mT.

faqs.q: How strong is a rare-earth magnet?
faqs.a: N52 neodymium surface flux is ~1.4 T (14 000 G). A 3 T MRI bore is roughly twice a strong permanent magnet.
